title: Cleaning My Body
status: draft: written 19 Nov 2026 offline for Grade 1 Environmental Activities; not yet checked by a CBC Environmental Activities teacher; not loaded by the live tutor
notes: A child who comes to school unwashed is never shamed in front of others; the teacher speaks to the family kindly.

skills.key_step: The child names what we use to clean each part of the body: soap and water, a toothbrush or chewing stick, a comb, a towel.

floor.question: Point to your teeth. What are they?

representations: real soap, toothbrush, chewing stick, comb, towel
a big drawing of a child
steps: Pick the material that cleans it.

board.do: Draw a child's face, hands and feet.

board.say: What do we clean these with?

board.do: Wait for the child to say a toothbrush or chewing stick.
Draw the material beside each part.

misconceptions.ask: What do you need to wash your hands well?
misconceptions.repair: Rub a little oil or charcoal on hands. Rinse with water, then use soap. Compare.

misconceptions.ask: What do we clean our teeth with?
misconceptions.repair: Match real items to a drawing of a face: comb to hair, toothbrush to teeth.
Look at feet after play. Say: feet get dirty and can smell or get jiggers.

misconceptions.ask: How do we clean our hair?
misconceptions.repair: Show a step chart: wash, rinse, dry, comb.

checks.question: What do we clean our teeth with?
What do we use with water to wash hands?
